evidence.notes: Both builds keep the backend contract and test selectors intact, derive controls from allowedActions, serialize versioned mutations and handle STALE_VERSION and partial sources, and both adopt a checklist-first hire workspace with PII hidden on demand. Y is materially stronger on governed actions and state truthfulness: approve/reject go through a consequence-stating confirm step and every successful mutation yields a server-confirmed, versioned receipt, whereas X executes decisions on one click with no receipt. Y also recomposes cleanly at every width (including moving approvals above the checklist on mobile) while X overflows at 768 and has an awkward desktop table. X has the better default prioritisation (needs-attention sort, 'Waiting on you' grouping) and a cleaner axe result, but overall Y is the more complete and robust result.

scorer_rationale.task_hierarchy: Hires list defaults to 'Needs attention first' sort with clickable status counts; hire page leads with attention chips (awaiting you / exceptions / blocked / overdue) and a main column of Issues + Checklist; manager page groups 'Waiting on you' first.
scorer_rationale.domain_adaptation: Checklist-first workspace in dependency order (lib/checklist.ts dependencyOrder) with owner/due/overdue/depends-on and approval linkage; PII shown once, hidden until revealed and only for HR partners; unavailable document vault explained as 'not missing'.
scorer_rationale.contract_preservation: No src/api or src/mock changes; hire-row, cohort-filter, task-checkbox preserved; status filter passed to server; controls derived from allowedActions. Adds a UI-only role policy hiding PII from managers (HirePage.tsx `me.role === 'hr_partner'`) and a SessionGate that blocks the whole app when /api/me fails.
scorer_rationale.interaction_state: Loading, empty, no-match, read-only, 403/404, partial (unavailableSources), STALE_VERSION pause with 'Load latest version' and inline mutation errors are handled; but error scenario collapses to a single 'Could not load your session' screen, there is no success receipt except 'Request sent.', and approve/reject execute on one click with no confirm step.
scorer_rationale.responsive: 375 recomposes the table into labelled cards with no overflow, but verify.json shows primary@768 pageOverflowX (table right=805, header clipped) and the table wraps dates to 4 lines at 1440; detail page does not reorder approvals ahead of the 10-task checklist on mobile.
scorer_rationale.accessibility: axe clean on primary and detail, 29-30 tab stops all focus-visible (3px outline), no unnamed controls, labelled checkboxes and selects, progressbar with valuetext, text+glyph status badges, reduced-motion rule; no skip link.
scorer_rationale.visual_consistency: Calm, restrained tokens and badges, but the desktop table is poorly proportioned (start date column wraps heavily) and each task shows a status badge plus a redundant status select, adding noise.
scorer_rationale.maintainability: Clean feature folders, HireContext with a single serialized `run` mutation helper, useResource, lib/checklist hints and describeError; 18 new tests including stale-version recovery.
scorer_rationale.ai_governance: Only the named approver sees Approve/Reject, reject requires a comment, decision disabled until dependencies are done, server response replaces state; but no confirmation step naming consequences (reject blocks the task and hire) and no decision receipt.

overfitting.dominant_ia: filterable cohort table -> hire workspace (checklist + issues main column, approvals/documents/PII side rail) + mobile card list for manager summary

manager 'Waiting on you' grouping with next action/owner/due
